public.title: Serialize and Deserialize Binary Tree
public.description: Trees use compact breadth-first arrays: the root comes first, then the left and right children of each non-null node in queue order; null means absent and trailing nulls may be omitted. Empty arrays mean no root. For "serialize", return the canonical compact breadth-first array as JSON without spaces. For "deserialize", accept that JSON string and return the canonical array. Remove trailing nulls and normalize an absent root to []. Inputs represent valid trees with at most 500 nodes and integer values between -10000 and 10000. This value-only codec contract fixes the encoding rather than testing object identity.
public.attribution: Original statement, examples, tests and solutions authored for Bekor, 2026. Uses a standard algorithmic pattern; no third-party exercise text used.

explanation: Canonicalization removes trailing absence markers while retaining internal ones; JSON supplies the unambiguous number/null framing. O(n) time and space.
